business_scope.primary_industry_name: Electronic Retailing of Pet Supplies and Pet Care Devices

meta_jurisdiction_context.legal_system_doctrine: Hybrid: Civil law (Civil Code of Quebec, CQLR c. CCQ-1991) governs private law; common law governs federal public and criminal law; corporate law is provincial statutory law under the Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1.
applicable_bilateral_investment_treaties: CPTPP (Comprehensive and Progressive Agreement for Trans-Pacific Partnership, 2018)
CETA (Canada-European Union Comprehensive Economic and Trade Agreement, 2017)
Canada-United States Tax Convention (1980, as amended)

ubo_and_aml_profiling.statutory_law_governance: Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, S.C. 2000, c. 17 (PCMLTFA), including FINTRAC KYC/CDD obligations imposed on regulated financial intermediaries (banks and payment service providers such as Stripe and PayPal); Criminal Code, R.S.C., 1985, c. C-46, Part XII.2 (offence of laundering proceeds of crime); Quebec Business Corporations Act, CQLR c. S-31.1, s. 92 (obligation to maintain an internal register of individuals with significant control); An Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, CQLR c. P-44.1, ss. 1.2.5 and 22.1 et seq. (mandatory filing of the UBO register and controlling-information updates with the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec); Regulation respecting fees payable to the Registraire des entreprises du Quebec, CQLR c. P-44.1, r. 1.

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Incorporation (Certificat de constitution) issued under the Quebec Business Corporations Act
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Global Affairs Canada or Ministere de la Justice du Quebec

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Articles of Incorporation (Statuts de constitution) and attested by-laws
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: REQ and corporate secretary / Quebec lawyer or notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Register of Individuals with Significant Control (Registre des personnes ayant un controle important) extract, including UBO name, date of birth, jurisdiction, and nature of control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Company corporate secretary, attested by a Quebec notary

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Notarized copies of government-issued photo identification (passport pages) of each director, officer, and individual with significant control
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.issuing_entity: Notary in the applicant's country of origin
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille (or consular legalization only if the country of origin is not a party to the Hague Apostille Convention)

mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.document_name: Certificate of Compliance / Good Standing (Attestation de conformite) from the REQ
mandatory_notarization_and_apostille_bun.authentication_path: Hague Apostille via Ministere de la Justice du Quebec

ubo_and_aml_profiling.pep_and_sanctions_screening_protocols: Mandatory screening of all proposed directors, officers, UBOs, and authorized signing parties against: (i) FINTRAC politically exposed persons (PEP) and Heads of International Organizations definitions under PCMLTFA and FINTRAC Guidance 4; (ii) Canadian sanctions lists under the Special Economic Measures Act, S.C. 1992, c. 17, the United Nations Act, R.S.C., 1985, c. U-2, and the Justice for Victims of Corrupt Foreign Officials Act, S.C. 2011, c. 31, s. 155; (iii) OFAC SDN and UN Consolidated List references as applied by U.S. payment rails; and (iv) enhanced due diligence is not triggered for this low-risk e-commerce tier, but negative-news and global-watchlist screening is required prior to incorporation and at each UBO-register update.

statutory_name_clearance_protocol.registry_portal_name: Registraire des entreprises du Quebec (REQ) online portal: https://www.registreentreprises.gouv.qc.ca (transactional platform for name reservation, NUANS filing, and incorporation).
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.language_and_transliteration_doctrine: Under the Charter of the French Language, CQLR c. C-11, and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises, the corporate name must be in French. A bilingual name is permitted only where the non-French element is a recognized proper noun, a distinctive mark, or an approved legal element such as 'Inc.' or 'Societe par actions'. Non-French commercial names require prior authorization from the Office quebecois de la langue francaise in limited cases. Transliteration into Latin script with French grammatical structure is mandatory; numerals and Roman-letter acronyms are acceptable if linguistically compliant.
statutory_name_clearance_protocol.extension_and_rejection_appeal_sop: If the REQ refuses a proposed name, the applicant receives a written reasoned decision. The applicant may (i) file a new name reservation with a fresh NUANS report within the original 90-day window, or (ii) submit a written request for reconsideration to the REQ within 30 days of refusal. A final administrative appeal may be filed with the Tribunal administratif du Quebec within 30 days of a second refusal, and judicial review is available before the Superior Court of Quebec. Practical expedient: amend and resubmit a linguistically compliant name immediately, as appeal processes typically exceed the 90-day reservation validity.

registered_office_and_commercial_substan.virtual_office_permissibility: Permissible for this low-risk e-commerce retailer only if the registered office is a physical street address in Quebec capable of receiving service of process and official REQ/CRA correspondence during normal business hours. A post office box or a purely virtual digital address is not compliant with section 42 of the QBCA and the Act respecting the legal publicity of enterprises. Registered-agent address services in Montreal, Quebec City, or Laval are commonly accepted.
registered_office_and_commercial_substan.physical_inspection_likelihood: Quantified risk of unannounced physical on-site inspection is low, estimated at approximately 5-8% probability during the first 12 months for a digitally domiciled, low-risk e-commerce entity operating through Stripe and PayPal. Inspection risk materially increases if GST/QST remittances are late, consumer complaints are filed with the Office de la protection du consommateur, or the payment processors file suspicious-transaction reports referencing the corporation's Business Number.

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.legal_fee_basis: Statutory tariff and prevailing market rate CAD 25-30

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Registered office / virtual business address service, first year
pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.charging_authority: Corporate services provider / registered-agent firm in Quebec

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Legal fees for drafting articles, by-laws, minute book, UBO/ISC register, and director residency review
Notarization of UBO, director, and officer identification documents
Hague Apostille authentication of corporate certificates (3 documents)

pre_incorporation_itemized_budget_usd.expense_line_item: Certified French translation and linguistic compliance review of articles and supporting documents
Initial annual declaration update (declaration annuelle, year 1)

incorporation_legal_framework.governing_statute_and_sections: Business Corporations Act (Québec), CQLR c. S-31.1 (QBCA); applicable sections include 5(1) (incorporation by articles), 8 (content of articles), 10 (corporate name), 36 (registered office), 43 (share consideration), 53 (first directors), 64 (bylaws), 66 (standard of care), and 161 (officers).
incorporation_legal_framework.competent_registry_authority: Registraire des entreprises, Gouvernement du Québec; electronic filing through the Registraire's authorized online filing portal.
incorporation_legal_framework.statutory_filing_instrument: Articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs) filed in the form prescribed by the Registraire des entreprises, together with the required declaration for registration in the Quebec Enterprise Register.
incorporation_legal_framework.minimum_paid_up_capital_rule: No statutory minimum paid-up capital is required for incorporation under the QBCA. Shares may be issued without a minimum allotment, and no escrow or bank deposit undertaking is required. Each share must be issued for consideration approved by the directors, being money, property, or past service.
incorporation_legal_framework.pro_forma_first_board_resolution_en: RESOLVED THAT, subject to the Articles of Incorporation filed with the Registraire des entreprises, this corporation accepts the subscriptions of the subscribers listed in the subscription schedule and confirms the allotment of shares in consideration paid or to be paid; and the directors are authorized to issue share certificates accordingly. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT the registered office of the corporation is established at [address], Province of Quebec, until changed by resolution; the directors authorize the filing of the registered office notice and the opening of corporate bank accounts with approved signatories. RESOLVED FURTHER THAT [name] is appointed President, [name] is appointed Secretary, and [name] is appointed Treasurer, each to serve until removed; these appointments take effect immediately.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Corporate Name Search and Name Reservation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises – online name search and reservation service (NUANS / demande de réservation de nom).
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Conduct a NUANS name search through the Registraire's authorized service channel. Submit a name reservation request for up to three proposed corporate names in order of preference. Ensure the selected name contains the required legal element such as Inc., Corp., or Ltée. If the name is descriptive or non-distinctive, attach an explanatory memorandum to support administrative approval.
required_dossiers: NUANS report dated within 90 days
Name reservation request form completed and signed
Explanatory letter for distinctive or descriptive names, if required
Payment receipt for name search and reservation fees
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the name reservation is refused, the registry will issue a technical refusal notice. Submit a revised request with an adjusted corporate name, or file a reconsideration request with the Registraire's legal information directorate within 30 days, attaching supplementary evidence of distinctiveness.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Preparation and Execution of Articles of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises – integrated electronic articles preparation module; Quebec legal counsel or authorized filing agent if desired.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Draft the articles of incorporation in accordance with QBCA s. 8. The articles must state the corporate name, the province of Quebec as the registered office jurisdiction, the first directors, the share structure and any restrictions on share transfers or business activities. Each incorporator must sign the articles, and each first director must sign a consent to act as director. Verify that the registered office municipal address is included if required by the Registraire's validation rules.
required_dossiers: Signed articles of incorporation (statuts constitutifs)
Name reservation confirmation
Consent to act as director from each first director
Identity documents for each incorporator
Completed incorporator information schedule
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the Registraire returns the articles for correction, use the online filing workspace to cure validation errors or missing consents and resubmit without a new fee if done within the stated correction period. If the issue is substantive, amend the articles and obtain all required signatures again before re-filing.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Electronic Filing and Issuance of Certificate of Incorporation
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises – secure online filing portal for constitutions.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Upload the executed articles into the Registraire's electronic filing system, pay the prescribed filing fee by accepted electronic payment method, and transmit the application. The Registraire reviews the file for compliance with the QBCA. Upon approval, the company is constituted and registered in the Quebec Enterprise Register, and the Registraire issues the attestation of constitution and enterprise number (NEQ).
required_dossiers: Articles of incorporation in electronic PDF format
Name reservation receipt
Digital signature authorization or e-signature record
Payment receipt for constitution filing fee
Consent forms of first directors
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the application is queried or rejected, review the Registraire's written notice, correct the specified deficiencies, and resubmit through the online portal. If a legal interpretation is required, attach a signed opinion of Quebec counsel to the curative filing. If the fee is insufficient, remit the balance before resubmission.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Establishment of Registered Office and Corporate Records
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Registraire des entreprises; corporate records maintained at the registered office in Quebec.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Notify the Registraire of the exact municipal address of the registered office and maintain the statutory minute book at that address. The records must include the articles, bylaws, minutes of meetings, securities register, and registers of directors and shareholders. Issue share certificates once the board has accepted the share subscriptions and determined that consideration is fully or partially received as permitted by the QBCA.
required_dossiers: Notice of registered office address
Lease agreement, ownership title, or owner's consent for the office address
Minute book and corporate records binder
Register of directors and register of shareholders
Blank share certificates and corporate seal
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the notice of registered office is rejected due to address formatting or geocoding problems, resubmit the notice using the municipal address recognized by the local land registry and attach the owner's consent or lease excerpt confirming the unit number. If the registry requests supporting documents, upload them promptly.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Adoption of Bylaws and First Board Resolution
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Board of directors of the corporation acting under the QBCA.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Convene a first meeting of the board or execute a unanimous written resolution. The directors must approve the general operating bylaw (By-law No. 1), confirm share subscriptions, fix the registered office, approve banking resolutions, and appoint the president, secretary, and treasurer or other officers. Minutes or resolution records must be entered in the corporate minute book and signed by the chair and secretary.
required_dossiers: Notice of first board meeting or waiver of notice
Pro-forma first board resolution
By-law No. 1 (general operating bylaw)
Share subscription schedule and evidence of consideration
Officer acceptance and consent forms
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If a procedural defect is later discovered, the directors may adopt a curative unanimous resolution ratifying the prior acts and approving all decisions taken at the first meeting. Record the curative resolution in the minute book and re-file any registry notices if necessary.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Mandatory Tax and Payroll Registrations with Federal and Quebec Authorities
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Revenu Québec and Canada Revenue Agency; business number registration.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: After constitution, register the corporation with Revenu Québec for the Quebec sales tax (QST), source deductions, and any applicable employer accounts. Apply to the Canada Revenue Agency for a business number and GST/HST account for federal sales tax. The enterprise number (NEQ) assigned by the Registraire should be used consistently in all filings, and a physical place of business address in Quebec must be confirmed for tax correspondence.
required_dossiers: Attestation de constitution from the Registraire
First board resolution and officer appointment minutes
Directors' identification and proof of authority
Registered office and warehouse address details
Estimated revenue and payroll projections for registration questionnaires
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If Revenu Québec issues a notice of discrepancy or requests additional information, respond through the Revenu Québec online business account with a completed RC1W form or provincial equivalent. Correct the registration fields and provide the requested organizational documents within 30 days to avoid account suspension.

step_by_step_formation_sop.step_name: Municipal Zoning, Fire Safety, and Physical Premises Clearance
step_by_step_formation_sop.competent_authority: Local municipality (e.g., Ville de Montréal or applicable MRC), local fire prevention service, and CNESST.
step_by_step_formation_sop.detailed_action_protocol: Obtain a municipal business permit, zoning certificate, or occupancy authorization for the administrative office and fulfillment warehouse. Arrange a fire safety inspection of the premises. For warehouse racking systems, provide structural certification if required by the Quebec building code. If employees will work in the premises, register the employer with CNESST for occupational health and safety coverage and post the required workplace notices.
required_dossiers: Municipal business permit or zoning authorization application
Certificate of occupancy or lease approval
Fire safety plan and inspection record
Structural load certificate for industrial racking, if applicable
CNESST employer registration confirmation
step_by_step_formation_sop.adverse_action_remedies: If the municipality or fire service identifies deficiencies, obtain a written correction notice, complete the required remediation, and request a re-inspection within the specified period. If zoning refusal is based on land use regulations, file an administrative appeal with the municipality or the competent municipal administrative tribunal.

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.competent_industrial_authority: Not applicable for ISIC 4791 electronic retailing of pet supplies and pet care devices; no provincial industrial licence is required. For physical premises, the relevant local municipal inspection service, the local fire prevention service, and the Commission des normes, de l'équité, de la santé et de la sécurité du travail (CNESST) have jurisdiction.
industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.operating_license_title: No provincial occupation or operating licence is required under Quebec's licensing framework for pure e-commerce retailing of pet supplies. A municipal business permit and occupancy certificate for the warehouse and office premises are the required administrative authorizations.

environmental_impact_assessment_eia.agency_name: Ministère de l'Environnement, de la Lutte contre les changements climatiques, de la Faune et des Parcs (MELCCFP).
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.classification_tier: Exempt – a full environmental impact assessment is not triggered for a warehouse-based retail distribution operation. If the premises later introduce manufacturing, pet food processing, or hazardous substance storage, a voluntary attestation or registration under the Quebec Environment Quality Act may become necessary.
environmental_impact_assessment_eia.discharge_and_emissions_standards: No process wastewater, VOCs, or industrial air emissions are expected from dry pet supplies storage and fulfillment activities. Any sanitary and storm water discharges must comply with municipal sewer bylaws and the Quebec Regulation respecting municipal wastewater treatment works; residual solid waste must be managed under the Residual Materials Management Regulation (Q-2, r. 46).

industry_physical_and_environmental_lice.civil_defense_and_occupational_clearance: The physical premises require a fire safety inspection and occupancy certificate under the Quebec Fire Safety Code and local municipal by-laws. Structural load certification may be required for high-density warehouse racking. Employer workplace clearance and health and safety obligations are enforced by CNESST under the Act respecting occupational health and safety, CQLR c. S-2.1, including worker training and first-aid requirements.

national_tax_registration_infrastructure.competent_tax_authority: Canada Revenue Agency / Agence du revenu du Canada (CRA-ARC); federal portal 'My Business Account' (https://www.canada.ca/en/revenue-agency/services/e-services/digital-services-businesses.html). Quebec counterpart: Revenu Québec (https://www.revenuquebec.ca), administering the Quebec Sales Tax (QST/TVQ) and Quebec corporate income tax under the Taxation Act (Loi sur les impôts).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.tax_id_procurement_sop: A foreign business corporation engaged in e-commerce in Quebec must obtain a federal 9-digit Business Number (BN) with a GST/HST account through CRA Business Registration Online (BRO) or Form RC1/RC143; non-residents use Form RC413. The BN is the national TIN. The corporation must also register with Revenu Québec through 'Mon dossier d'entreprise' using the enterprise's NEQ (Numéro d'entreprise du Québec) from the Registraire des entreprises du Québec to open a QST account; an import/export account may be added if goods are imported for Canadian fulfilment. Non-resident applicants must submit certified constitutional documents, proof of foreign registration, a Canadian fiscal representative appointment where required, and evidence of Quebec nexus (place of business, resident agent, or warehouse/fulfilment centre).
national_tax_registration_infrastructure.statutory_election_mechanisms: Canada does not operate a US-style 'check-the-box' regime; a business corporation is always taxed at the entity level. Available elections: functional currency election under Income Tax Act (ITA) s. 261; GST/HST closely related corporation election under ETA s. 156; QST joint election under s. 196.1 of the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax (deemed nil consideration for intercompany supplies); and non-resident rental income election under ITA s. 216. Hybrid mismatch rules under ITA ss. 18.2–18.4 address BEPS Action 2 structures and are not elective, though taxpayers may make timing adjustments through structured arrangement disclaimers.

indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.indirect_tax_system_name: GST/HST (Goods and Services Tax / Harmonized Sales Tax) and QST (Quebec Sales Tax) — VAT-style consumption taxes
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.statutory_registration_threshold_local_c: CAD 30,000 annual taxable-supplies threshold for both GST/HST and QST (small-supplier rule). Once worldwide taxable supplies to Canadian persons exceed CAD 30,000 in a calendar quarter, foreign e-commerce vendors must register for GST/HST; once Quebec taxable supplies exceed CAD 30,000, registration for QST is required. Combined Quebec rate is 14.975% (GST 5% + QST 9.975%). Non-resident vendors with goods delivered from Canadian fulfilment centres or sold through online platforms are deemed to carry on business in Canada for GST/HST purposes and must register before the threshold is exceeded. Registration is prospective and idempotent.
indirect_taxation_nexus_and_rules.electronic_invoicing_and_clearance_manda: Canada has no real-time fiscal clearance, government invoicing stamping, or publication-service API clearance regime. CRA mandates electronic filing of GST/HST returns for registrants with annual taxable supplies exceeding CAD 10,000; Revenu Québec mandates electronic filing and remittance for GST/HST/QST above prescribed thresholds. Commercial e-invoices must be retained in machine-readable format (XML or PDF) for 7 years. Since 2024, payment service providers including Stripe and PayPal are subject to ETA Part V.1 registration and annual reporting obligations regarding foreign merchants. Online marketplace operators are deemed to make taxable supplies and must collect tax at source when vendors sell through a marketplace such as Amazon. No pre-clearance stamping or government invoice validation applies in Quebec.

export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.zero_rating_eligibility: Zero-rating under ETA Schedule VI, Part V and the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax (ss. 100 ff.) applies where goods are exported by the supplier in the ordinary course of business, title passes to a non-resident recipient, and shipment is made to a destination outside Canada. For e-commerce pet-product exports, each sale must be made to a non-resident person, physically exported via common carrier, and supported with contemporaneous export documentation. Services supplied to non-residents qualify where performed wholly outside Canada or substantially related to foreign property. Intangible supplies electronically delivered to non-residents are zero-rated as well. Claiming 0% GST/HST/QST requires the vendor to hold reasonable evidence of export at or before the time of filing the return for the reporting period.
mandatory_customs_documentation_bundle: Canada Customs Export Declaration (Form B13A) or CBSA-approved low-value export entry, or carrier-reported electronic export information for courier consignments
Bill of Lading, Air Waybill, or Canada Post/courier label showing Canadian origin and foreign destination address
Commercial invoice (HS classification, quantity, unit price in CAD, Incoterms, country of destination, seller and buyer identification)
Carrier proof of delivery or customs clearance certificate confirming arrival in the destination country
Inward Remittance Certificate, SWIFT/MT103 credit advice, or merchant-platform payout statement evidencing receipt of export proceeds from the foreign buyer
Export-warehouse and order-fulfilment documentation (picking slips, courier manifests, and import-export statistics reports where applicable)
export_zero_rating_and_refund_substantia.audit_scrutiny_and_clawback_penalties: CRA and Revenu Québec may reassess GST/HST and QST within 4 years of an assessment, or without time limit in cases of misrepresentation or fraud. Improper zero-rating triggers reassessment at 14.975% combined, daily compound prescribed interest, and penalties: ETA s. 285 failure-to-remit penalty (greater of CAD 250 and 10% of net tax), ETA s. 280 gross-negligence false-reporting penalty (greater of CAD 100 and 50% of the tax unreported), and the mirror QST penalty provisions under the Act respecting the Quebec Sales Tax. Criminal prosecution for fraudulent export zero-rating may result in fines up to 200% of tax evaded and imprisonment up to 5 years. Documentary insufficiency, split shipments to domestic intermediate addresses, or absence of evidence of foreign-currency proceeds within 180 days will trigger clawback of zero-rating and recharacterisation of the supply as taxable domestic; Revenu Québec applies analogous administrative fines and may exclude habitual non-compliant exporters from simplified reporting programs.

fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.central_bank_authority: Bank of Canada (Banque du Canada), in coordination with the Office of the Superintendent of Financial Institutions (OSFI) for bank prudential oversight, FINTRAC for anti-money-laundering and counter-terrorist-financing supervision, and the Autorité des marchés financiers (AMF) for Quebec financial-services conduct.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.currency_convertibility_assessment: Canada is an IMF Article VIII member; the Canadian dollar (CAD) is fully convertible for both current-account and capital-account transactions. The federal Exchange Control era has been repealed, so no government authorization is required for the inflow or outflow of capital, dividends, interest, royalties, shareholder loans, or e-commerce sales revenues. The Quebec corporation may hold CAD, USD, and other foreign-currency accounts at a Canadian chartered bank. Profit remittance to non-resident shareholders is subject only to standard withholding taxes under Part XIII of the Income Tax Act and relevant double-tax agreements, not to FX control. No stamp duty, exchange permit, or pre-approval applies. The only practical hurdle is bank-level due diligence demonstrating that funds are legitimate and not routed through sanctioned jurisdictions.
fx_control_regime_and_central_bank_regul.export_proceeds_surrender_rules: None. Canada imposes no statutory requirement for exporters to surrender foreign currency to the central bank or to any government agency, nor does it set a mandatory timeline or minimum conversion ratio for export receipts. A Quebec pet-supplies retailer may benefit from foreign-exchange gains and retain foreign currency in trade accounts; however, the Income Tax Act requires that inventory purchases and revenues be reported in Canadian dollars at the Bank of Canada daily exchange rate for tax filings. Exports of pet products are not subject to special surrender or conversion formalities, but all cross-border receipts must be documented for Canadian customs lodgment and sales-tax (GST/HST/QST) reporting.

corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.fintech_emi_cross_border_viability: Medium (supporting role only). Canadian law does not adopt the European EMI licence; offshore electronic-money institutions cannot take deposits or provide full banking facilities in Canada without a Canadian bank charter. A non-resident fintech may operate as a FINTRAC-registered money service business (MSB) for payment processing under the Proceeds of Crime (Money Laundering) and Terrorist Financing Act, and as a registered payment service provider under the new Retail Payment Activities Act (RPAA) once fully effective. For the Québec e-commerce entity, platforms such as Stripe, PayPal, Wise, and Airwallex are permissible as secondary settlement rails for online retail sales, but the primary treasury account must be held with a Canadian Schedule I bank to ensure sovereign deposit protection and reliable clearance through Lynx/ACH. Offshore EMIs should not custody the operational liquidity of a Canadian operating corporation.
corporate_banking_onboarding_blueprint.physical_presence_and_kyc_interview_mand: Remote opening is generally permissible at the major Canadian banks for a Quebec-incorporated corporation when all directors and Ultimate Individual Owners (UIOs) can be identified online or through a notarized agent. A video interview is typically required for at least one director who holds signing authority. Physical presence in a branch is not mandatory under FINTRAC customer due diligence rules, but many banks require a wet-ink signature on the account-opening mandate and a Quebec-registered address that is a physical place of business or a registered agent office. For a wholly foreign-owned Quebec corporation, the bank will expect the foreign director’s passport, proof of residential address, and a valid certificate of corporate status. The bank may require that the Quebec-raised director or a locally resident corporate officer have signing authority to expedite opening.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Beneficial ownership opacity because the company is controlled by non-resident individuals through a foreign holding structure.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Provide the corporate registry extract from Registraire des entreprises du Québec (REQ) showing the legal name, jurisdiction, and directors; a detailed beneficial-ownership register capturing each individual with 25% or more ultimate ownership trade; the trust deed or corporate-organizational chart for each intermediate layer; notarized copies of passports and proof of address for all UIOs; resolution of shareholders authorizing the bank account; and a written attestation of source of wealth.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: High-volume e-commerce revenue with numerous micro-payment settlements from Stripe and PayPal, triggering 'unsigned and manually unverifiable' transaction patterns.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Submit processor monthly settlement statements (Stripe/PayPal) clearly identifying net sales, refunds, chargebacks, and platform fees; a copy of the e-commerce website and product listings (NAICS 459910); logistics evidence from UPS/FedEx/Canada Post; wholesale supplier invoices; and a board-approved cash-flow forecast. The bank may also require read-only API access to the payment processor for a trial customer-verification period.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Large inbound capital injection from a non-resident parent or shareholder loan, potentially characterized as suspicious or lacking economic rationale.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Deliver an executed shareholder loan agreement or equity subscription agreement with defined terms, repayment schedule, and purpose; source-of-funds documentation from the remitting institution (bank statements for the prior 3–6 months, sale-and-purchase agreements, or audited financial statements of the lender); a constitutional resolution of the Quebec corporation approving the injection; and a business plan detailing the use of proceeds for inventory, marketing, and operating costs.

critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.trigger_point: Sanctions or politically exposed person (PEP) flags connected to a shareholder, director, or jurisdiction of payment routing.
critical_aml_kyc_blockers_and_defense.evidentiary_defense_dossier: Prepare an independent legal opinion obtained from a Canadian counsel confirming that the transaction is not prohibited under the United Nations Act, the Special Economic Measures Act, or Canadian sanctions regulations administered by Global Affairs Canada; axe a sworn affidavit from the flagged individual itemizing the relationship, source of funds, and absence of PEP status where true; and route all initial funding through a Canadian-regulated bank account from a permissible jurisdiction. The bank may require enhanced monitoring for a defined term.

cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.inbound_capital_injection_routing: For a Quebec-incorporated entity receiving parent-company equity or shareholder loan from abroad, the compliant rail is a SWIFT MT103 wire transfer to the Canadian bank account. The beneficiary account is the corporate Operational Account or a designated Capital Escrow sub-account. Field 70 (Remittance Information) must identify the economic nature, e.g., 'Share capital contribution' or 'Shareholder loan' to permit accurate book/tax characterization. Canadian banks do not use official exchange-control purpose codes, but the bank will require supporting documents on file: board resolution, share subscription agreement, loan agreement, and proof of source of funds. The bank will verify that the remitting financial institution is not on any sanctions list, and if the incoming currency is not CAD, the bank executes the conversion at its prevailing commercial exchange rate. For sums above CAD 10,000, the bank must file an Electronic Funds Transfer Report (EFTR) with FINTRAC, and in cases of large or unusual transactions, it may request the Beneficial Ownership Register and source-of-wealth evidence.
cross_border_liquidity_and_clearing_rail.outbound_trade_disbursements: Routine operating disbursements, including supplier payments, warehousing fees, and refunds, are cleared through the Canadian payment system: the high-value Lynx system for SWIFT MT103 and domestic CAD wire; the retail Automated Clearing Settlement System (ACSS) for EFT and bill payments; and card-network rails for Stripe/PayPal disbursements. For international trade settlements with overseas vendors of pet products, the primary rail is SWIFT MT103 (telegraphic transfer) with the invoice reference in the remittance field. For larger purchases (typically above CAD 50,000 total risk) where the vendor requires a bank undertaking, an irrevocable Commercial Letter of Credit (LC) drawn under UCP 600 is permissible, opened by the Canadian bank in favour of the supplier. The LC route guarantees payment against compliant shipping documents (commercial invoice, bill of lading, packing list, and certificate of origin). All outbound payments are subject to Canadian sanctions screening and must correspond to legitimate business expenses; no FX permit or authorization is required for these disbursements.
permissible_fx_hedging_instruments: Outright FX Forward Contracts (physically settled USDCAD/EURCAD/GBPCAD and other deliverable pairs) with a Canadian chartered bank as counterparty
Non-Deliverable Forwards (NDFs) for currencies not legally deliverable in Canada, such as certain emerging-market exotic pairs, assuming prudent underlying exposure and bank approval
FX Swaps (single-day or short-term swaps) involving simultaneous spot and forward exchange of principal, used for temporary liquidity needs
Cross-Currency Interest Rate Swaps (CCIRS) to manage combined interest-rate and currency risk on foreign-currency borrowings
European-style Plain Vanilla FX Options (calls/puts) on major currency pairs purchased for hedging purposes, avoiding speculative uncovered option writing

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Federal annual return and individuals with significant control information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.receiving_authority: Corporations Canada, Innovation, Science and Economic Development Canada
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Annual return: within 60 days after the corporation's anniversary date. Initial and subsequent ISC information must be filed with the annual return and updated within 15 days after a change.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late or missing filings may result in compliance notices and administrative dissolution proceedings. A dissolved corporation loses its corporate status and may require restoration.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec annual updating declaration and ultimate-beneficiary information
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally filed annually during the statutory period following the corporation's fiscal year-end, ordinarily within six months after fiscal year-end; confirm the entity-specific deadline in the Québec enterprise register.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late filing may incur indexed administrative charges and compliance notices. Repeated failure to file may lead to ex officio dissolution or cancellation of registration after the prescribed statutory process.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Quebec corporate income tax return and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Any balance of tax is generally payable within two months after year-end, subject to applicable instalment rules.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Interest and late-filing penalties apply. Additional penalties may apply for unpaid instalments, repeated non-compliance, or failure to provide required information.

annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deliverable: Canadian federal corporate income tax return and related schedules
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.statutory_deadline_window: Generally within six months after the corporation's taxation year-end. Any balance of tax is generally payable within two months after year-end, subject to qualifying small-business corporation rules and instalment requirements.
annual_compliance_calendar_matrix.delinquency_sanctions: Late-filing penalties, arrears interest, instalment interest, and potential reassessment or collection action may apply.

statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.compulsory_audit_thresholds: For a federal private corporation, an auditor is generally appointed unless the shareholders unanimously resolve not to appoint one for the applicable financial year. Public companies and corporations subject to statutory securities reporting requirements require an independent auditor. Quebec requirements depend on the governing corporate statute, securities status, shareholder resolutions, financing covenants, and accounting or lender requirements; no universal revenue or asset threshold applies to every private corporation.
statutory_audit_and_accounting_mandate.governing_accounting_framework: Canadian private enterprises generally use Accounting Standards for Private Enterprises under Canadian GAAP. Entities with public accountability generally use IFRS as adopted in Canada. The selected framework must be applied consistently and supported by adequate financial records.

corporate_registers_and_ubo_annual_confi.ubo_annual_confirmation_protocol: Maintain current information on shareholders, control rights, and individuals with significant control or ultimate beneficiaries. For a federal corporation, file ISC information with the annual return and report changes to Corporations Canada within 15 days. For a Quebec-registered entity, report required ultimate-beneficiary information through the annual updating declaration and update material changes within the applicable statutory period. Record all share issuances, transfers, redemptions, and changes in control in the corporate registers and obtain required director or shareholder approvals.
mandatory_on_site_statutory_registers: Register of Individuals with Significant Control or Ultimate Beneficiaries
Articles, bylaws, shareholder resolutions, director resolutions, and filed corporate documents

recurring_annual_maintenance_budget_usd.statutory_audit_estimated_fee_usd: Approximately USD 3,000-15,000 for a small private corporation requiring an independent audit; review or compilation engagements are generally less costly but are not statutory audits.
